nodes.label: ReAct Framework
nodes.rationale: Reason + Act loop: each step consists of a reasoning step then an action step with tool calls

nodes.label: Agency Spectrum
nodes.rationale: Agency is a continuous spectrum from simple processors (no agency) to code agents (full agency)

nodes.label: Code Actions Paradigm
nodes.rationale: Writing LLM actions as code rather than JSON provides better composability, object management, generality, and representation in training data

nodes.label: Sandboxed Execution
nodes.rationale: Code execution requires sandboxed backends (E2B, Blaxel, Modal, Docker) for security; LocalPythonExecutor is not a security boundary

nodes.label: Multi-agent Systems
nodes.rationale: Specialized agents with separate tool sets and memories yield better benchmark performance than monolithic agents

nodes.label: Model-agnostic Design
nodes.rationale: smolagents supports any LLM: local transformers, ollama, inference providers, OpenAI, Anthropic via LiteLLM

nodes.label: Multi-step Agent Pattern
nodes.rationale: Agent runs in a loop executing actions until task is solved; each step can call tools

nodes.label: Human-in-the-Loop (HITL)
nodes.rationale: Enable human review and modification of agent plans before execution to ensure alignment with human intent

nodes.label: Agentic RAG
nodes.rationale: Agentic RAG overcomes limitations of single-step retrieval by enabling multi-step reasoning, query refinement, and self-critique

nodes.label: Text-to-SQL Agent
nodes.rationale: Agent can inspect SQL outputs and decide if queries need changing, providing robustness over standard text-to-SQL pipelines

nodes.label: Model-Agnostic Design
nodes.rationale: Any LLM (Hub Inference, OpenAI, Anthropic, local via Transformers/Ollama) can power an agent without code changes

nodes.label: Tool-Agnostic Design
nodes.rationale: Tools can come from MCP servers, LangChain, Hub Spaces, or custom implementations

nodes.label: OpenTelemetry Instrumentation
nodes.rationale: Standardized telemetry enables inspection and monitoring of multi-step agent runs which are inherently hard to debug

nodes.label: Code vs JSON Tool Calling Rationale
nodes.rationale: Code is superior to JSON for tool calls because of better composability (nesting, loops, conditionals), object management, generality, and representation in LLM training corpus
nodes.norm_label: code vs json tool calling rationale
